extracted.intended_audience: exporters, importers, respondents, and interested parties in BIS export-enforcement and Department of Commerce antidumping/countervailing duty proceedings (including trade counsel and company representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive legal requirements governing export-privilege denial orders and preliminary antidumping (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) determinations, including notice, disclosure, briefing, appeal, assessment, and suspension/liquidation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of export privileges under Section 1760(e) of ECRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Section 1760(e) of the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA), the export privileges of any person convicted of certain offenses (e.g., 18 U.S.C. 371, 18 U.S.C. 554) may be denied for a period of up to ten (10) years from the date of conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, any BIS-issued licenses or other authorizations in which the person had an interest at the time of the conviction may be revoked. Examples in the notice: seven-year and ten-year denial periods were imposed based on review of records and consultations with BIS Office of Exporter Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity for written submission (15 CFR 766.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: As provided in Section 766.25 of the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), BIS provides notice and opportunity for a convicted person to make a written submission to BIS before determining denial of export privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notices state BIS did provide such notice but had not received a written submission from the named individuals. Separate appeal rights also exist under Part 756.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on Denied Person participating in regulated transactions (Order - First)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the date of the Order until the specified expiration date, the Denied Person may not directly or indirectly participate in any way in any transaction involving any commodity, software or technology exported or to be exported from the United States that is subject to the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative prohibited acts enumerated: (A) applying for, obtaining, or using any license, license exception, or export control document; (B) carrying on negotiations concerning, ordering, buying, receiving, using, selling, delivering, storing, disposing of, forwarding, transporting, financing, or otherwise servicing any regulated item; (C) benefitting in any way from any transaction involving regulated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on third parties transacting with or for Denied Person (Order - Second)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may, directly or indirectly, do any of the following concerning the Denied Person: export/reexport/transfer to or on behalf of the Denied Person; facilitate the Denied Person's acquisition of ownership/possession/control of items; acquire from or facilitate acquisition from the Denied Person; obtain items from the Denied Person with knowledge they will be exported; engage in transactions to service items owned/controlled by the Denied Person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Servicing is defined for purposes of the Order as installation, maintenance, repair, modification, or testing. The clause covers financing or other support activities related to attempts to acquire items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope to reach related parties to prevent evasion (Order - Third)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority, any other person, firm, corporation, or business organization related to the Denied Person by ownership, control, position of responsibility, affiliation, or other connection in the conduct of trade or business may also be made subject to the provisions of the Order to prevent evasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits BIS to extend denial provisions to entities related to the denied individual when necessary to prevent circumvention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of denial Order (Part 756)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Part 756 of the Regulations, the Denied Person may file an appeal of the Order with the Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security. The appeal must be filed within 45 days from the date of the Order and must comply with Part 756.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice repeats the 45-day deadline and references Part 756 as the governing appeal procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and publication of Order (Order - Fifth)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the Order shall be delivered to the Denied Person and shall be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Federal Register is part of the Order's effect and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and duration of Orders (Order - Sixth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial Orders are effective immediately and shall remain in effect until a specified date (e.g., the notices specify orders remain in effect until May 19, 2030; December 19, 2033).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order text includes explicit start and end dates for the denial period tied to the conviction date or stated expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of administrative review when review request withdrawn (19 CFR 351.213(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.213(d)(1), Commerce will rescind an administrative review, in whole or in part, if the parties that requested the review withdraw their review requests within 90 days of the date of publication of the notice of initiation for the requested review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Nucor, SSAB Enterprises, and Cleveland-Cliffs withdrew requests for review of four companies within the 90-day deadline; Commerce rescinded the administrative review for those companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for AD administrative review (sections 751, 772, 773)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce conducts administrative reviews under sections 751(a)(1)(B) and (2) of the Tariff Act of 1930; export price and constructed export price are calculated in accordance with section 772 of the Act; normal value is calculated in accordance with section 773 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a full description, the notices point to the Preliminary Decision Memorandum available on ACCESS which explains the detailed calculation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of calculations for preliminary results (19 CFR 351.224(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to disclose the calculations and analysis performed to interested parties in the preliminary results within five days of the public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days after publication of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is normally required unless there are no calculations to disclose (e.g., total AFA used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case brief and rebuttal brief deadlines and content (19 CFR 351.309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties must submit case briefs no later than 21 days after publication of the notice; rebuttal briefs limited to issues raised in case briefs may be filed no later than five days after the date for filing case briefs. Briefs must include a table of contents listing each issue and a table of authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 19 CFR 351.309(c)(1)(ii), 351.309(d)(1), and 351.309(c)(2)/(d)(2) for content requirements and prior encouragements on executive summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public executive summary requirement and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce requests that interested parties provide at the beginning of their briefs a public executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs, limited to no more than 450 words per issue (not including citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce previously encouraged five-page executive summaries in prior proceedings; here the public executive summaries (with footnotes for citations) will be used as the basis of comment summaries in the issues and decision memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request procedure and content requirements (19 CFR 351.310(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties wishing to request a hearing must submit a written request to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance via ACCESS by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time within 30 days after publication of the notice. Hearing requests should contain: (1) party’s name, address, and telephone number; (2) number of participants and whether any participant is a foreign national; and (3) a list of issues to be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral presentations at the hearing will be limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal briefs; parties should confirm by telephone the date, time, and location two days before the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for final results of administrative review (section 751(a)(3)(A) and 19 CFR 351.213(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise extended, Commerce intends to issue the final results of the administrative review, including analysis of issues raised in written briefs, no later than 120 days after the date of publication of the preliminary notice in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines can be extended by Commerce under applicable rules and tolling memoranda are referenced in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment rate calculation and liquidation rules (19 CFR 351.212(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent’s weighted-average dumping margin is not zero or de minimis (less than 0.50 percent) in the final results, Commerce intends to calculate an importer-specific assessment rate based on the ratio of the total amount of dumping calculated for each importer’s examined sales and the total entered value of the sales in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the margin or importer-specific assessment rate is zero or de minimis in the final results, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to liquidate the appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation instructions for entries produced without knowledge of U.S. destination
rubrics_metrics.description: For entries of subject merchandise produced by individually examined respondents for which they did not know that the merchandise was destined to the United States, Commerce will instruct CBP to liquidate these entries at the all-others rate if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This governs situations involving intermediate companies and unknown U.S. destination knowledge by the producer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment for companies whose review was rescinded (19 CFR 351.212(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For companies for which the review is rescinded, Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries at a rate equal to the cash deposit of antidumping duties required at the time of entry, or withdrawal from warehouse, for consumption, during the POR in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(c)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce intends to issue these rescission instructions to CBP after publication of the preliminary notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of assessment instructions and effect of CIT summons
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions regarding individually examined respondents to CBP no earlier than 35 days after publication of the final results. If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (within 90 days of publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves judicial review opportunities before liquidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit requirement rules following final results
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication of final results, cash deposit requirements effective for shipments entered on or after the publication date: (1) individually examined respondents' deposit rate = rate in final results (unless <0.50% then zero); (2) for exporters not covered in this review but covered in a prior segment, continue to use the most recent company-specific rate; (3) if exporter not covered but producer is covered, use rate established for producer; (4) all other producers/exporters = all-others rate established in investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These deposit requirements remain in effect until further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer certificate requirement regarding reimbursement of duties (19 CFR 351.402(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Importers are reminded of their responsibility under 19 CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties prior to liquidation of relevant entries during the POR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply could result in Commerce’s presumption that reimbursement occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties, and/or an increase in antidumping duties by the amount of countervailing duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of facts available and adverse inferences (section 776)
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary information is missing from the record and respondents do not act to the best of their ability to respond, Commerce may rely on facts otherwise available and draw an adverse inference (AFA) where appropriate in selecting from among the facts available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Commerce applied total AFA to individually examined companies in the CVD investigation, which affected disclosure (no calculations to disclose) and led to preliminary subsidy rates based on AFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-others rate methodology for CVD investigations (sections 703(d) and 705(c)(5)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the preliminary determination, Commerce shall determine an estimated all-others rate for companies not individually examined equal to the weighted average of the estimated subsidy rates established for those companies individually examined, excluding zero and de minimis rates and rates based entirely on facts otherwise available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If individually examined rates are zero, de minimis, or based entirely on facts otherwise available, Commerce may use any reasonable method to establish the all-others rate pursuant to section 705(c)(5)(A)(ii). In the cited investigation Commerce established the all-others rate using the countervailable subsidy rate assigned to non-responsive companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of liquidation and cash deposit instruction for CVD preliminaries (section 703(d)(2) and 19 CFR 351.205(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with section 703(d)(2) of the Act, Commerce will direct CBP to suspend liquidation of entries of subject merchandise and, pursuant to 19 CFR 351.205(d), instruct CBP to require a cash deposit equal to the preliminary rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension and cash deposit take effect as of publication of the preliminary determination notice in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification may be omitted if respondents/government uncooperative
rubrics_metrics.description: If mandatory respondents did not participate and the government did not provide requested information, Commerce preliminarily determines the parties have been uncooperative and therefore verification will not be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce may instead rely on facts available and adverse inferences (AFA) in such circumstances; the notice explains this rationale for not conducting verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope comments procedure for investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Initiation Notice sets aside a period of time for parties to raise issues regarding product coverage (scope). Commerce intends to issue its preliminary decision regarding scope comments in the companion LTFV investigation and incorporate that scope decision into the final CVD determination after considering relevant scope case and rebuttal briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice references the Preamble and prior procedures and notes that deadlines for scope briefs will be established in the preliminary scope decision memorandum.
